gate: Gate: POST-PUBLISH TRIPWIRE, not a pre-publish gate (items 307-308 verdict, 2026-11-18). The clean split — build-only, verify, then publish the same dist/ — needs GoReleaser's `release --prepare` + `goreleaser publish`, which are GoReleaser Pro-only: the pinned OSS v2.20.2 binary has no `publish` command and rejects `--prepare` as an unknown flag (proven locally against the pinned binary). A second `release` run cannot publish the verified dist/ instead: `build` is not a skippable step and a run without --clean refuses an existing dist/, so it would wipe and rebuild — the published artifacts would be a rebuild, not the verified bits, re-signed with fresh per-run keyless certificates. Draft-release gating was rejected: it gates only the GitHub blobs, while the Docker image is pushed, signed and :latest-tagged in the same run before any verify, and a failed verify cannot un-push it. Manual `gh release create` + `docker push` + `cosign sign` re-publishing was rejected: it re-implements GoReleaser's publish pipe by hand with unpinned tooling and no local proof for the registry half. So the in-job `release verify` stays a post-publish tripwire by design: it fails the job, skips attestations and blocks the verify job, but it cannot un-publish. Measured locally 2026-11-18: two consecutive snapshot builds of the same committed tree produced different SHA-256 for all 12 archives + SBOMs, so a rebuild's bytes are provably not the verified bytes. Follow-up, not this slice: a GoReleaser Pro licence would unlock --prepare/publish (maintainer's call; not assumed). First CI execution still pending the first pushed tag.
